Kitchen, meals & drinks

mineral water noun

classical

Sen. N.Q. 3.25.9
Plin. N.H. 2.222 (medicātās aquās)
M-O s.v. mineral water

aqua medicāta

Examples

  • Lyncēstis aqua quae vocātur acidula vīnī modō temulentōs facit

    the Lyncestian water called acidula makes people drunk like winePlin. N.H. 2.230; cf. 31.9

Other words

  • aqua minerālis

    also used · modern · Traupman 72

    The modern term.

  • aqua acidula — acidulous mineral water

    also used · classical · Plin. N.H. 2.230; cf. 31.9

    Lewis & Short: “mineral water”. Pliny names such springs; he does not describe it as fizzy.

See also sparkling water, still water, spring water, tap water.

SourcesLewis & Short: medico · Lewis & Short: acidulus
